`abstention_correct` is {{v1.mean_abstention_correct|.1f}} for v1 and {{v2.mean_abstention_correct|.1f}} for v2 and v3: of the {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.n_unanswerable}} unanswerable questions, v1 refuses {{v1.n_abstained|count}} and v2 {{v2.n_abstained|count}}. The measured reason: with idf weighting their top retrieval scores range from {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.unanswerable_top_min|.4f}} to {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.unanswerable_top_max|.4f}}, while {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.answerable_at_or_below_max}} of the {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.n_answerable}} answerable questions score no higher than {{abl.abstention_separability.idf.unanswerable_top_max|.4f}}, so any `min_score` that rejects every unanswerable query also rejects most answerable ones (overlap weighting is no better: {{abl.abstention_separability.overlap.unanswerable_top_min|.4f}} to {{abl.abstention_separability.overlap.unanswerable_top_max|.4f}}, with {{abl.abstention_separability.overlap.answerable_at_or_below_max}} answerable questions at or below the top). Deciding answerability needs semantic matching, which a bag-of-words retriever cannot do. See `docs/design_faq.md`.
